chapter_title: Concerning the Five Things that he constructed with the hard Bodies of the Rulers
chapter_note: A very short, largely intact cosmological list-teaching: five cosmic constructions made by the Living Spirit from the hard bodies of the Rulers. The only clear late element is the formulaic dialogue/attribution opener in ¶1.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit constructed five great things from veins and skull[s in the] hard [bodies].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the hagiographic/dialogue frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks:" (Layer-2 compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological exposition (Living Spirit as cosmic artisan; construction-from-demon-bodies motif) preceded by a formulaic speaker-attribution, which marks later editorial framing.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the disc that is placed upon [the sh]oulder of the Porter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic numbered enumeration of cosmic architecture (item 1 of 5), staying entirely within the Manichaean cosmos (Porter as a cosmological being).

paragraphs.core_text: The se[con]d are the arches of [the] pillar that is before him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same impersonal, structural fivefold list; purely cosmic referents (pillar/arches) with no application to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird is the [mou]ld of the fo[r]m for the gehennas.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-mechanical itemization (a ‘mould/form’ for cosmic prisons), with lacunae preserved; no citations, exhortation, or institutional mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth are the [seven (?)] pillars that he has erected in the great sea, in [the] seven parts of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential-cosmological structuring (seven pillars; seven parts of the universe) in an expository register typical of the older teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth are the four walls that surround the vessels.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fivefold construction list; still ‘cosmos→cosmos’ description (walls/vessels as cosmic structures) without editorial application voice.
